subject: Biochemistry
vignette: A 4-year-old boy is diagnosed with Lesch-Nyhan syndrome after presenting with self-mutilation and hyperuricemia. His mother is healthy, but her brother has the same disorder, and her father is unaffected. She is pregnant with a male fetus and asks the pediatrician about the risk that this child will be affected.
question: Which of the following best describes the inheritance of this disorder?

options.text: Autosomal recessive, with a 25% risk for each child regardless of sex
Autosomal dominant, with a 50% risk for each child regardless of sex
X-linked dominant, with a 50% risk for all offspring of an affected mother
X-linked recessive, with a 50% risk for each male offspring of a carrier mother
Mitochondrial, with all offspring of an affected mother affected

explanation_correct: Lesch-Nyhan syndrome is caused by mutations in the HGPRT gene on the X chromosome and is inherited in an X-linked recessive pattern. An affected boy inherits the mutant allele from his carrier mother, who is typically unaffected; each son of a carrier mother has a 50% chance of being affected, and each daughter has a 50% chance of being a carrier. Father-to-son transmission does not occur.

explanation_incorrect.A: The disorder is X-linked, not autosomal recessive, so the recurrence risk differs by sex.
explanation_incorrect.B: Lesch-Nyhan syndrome is recessive; carrier mothers are clinically unaffected and there is no male-to-male transmission.
explanation_incorrect.C: An X-linked dominant disorder would affect carrier mothers, who are healthy in this family.
explanation_incorrect.E: The HGPRT gene is nuclear, not mitochondrial; mitochondrial inheritance would affect all children of an affected mother.

educationalObjective: Lesch-Nyhan syndrome is X-linked recessive, so each son of a carrier mother has a 50% risk of being affected.
